subsystems.name: Superposition layer
subsystems.role: creates an equal-weight superposition across all 2^n computational basis states.

subsystems.name: Phase-encoding layer
subsystems.role: imprints the Fourier kernel as binary-weighted phases on the superposition.
parts: controlled-phase gates with angles halving at each step
phase kickback from an ancilla register

subsystems.name: Qubit-order correction
subsystems.role: reverses the qubit order left by the recursive decomposition.
parts: or classical relabeling of measured bits

subsystems.name: Inverse QFT
subsystems.role: the adjoint circuit used inside quantum phase estimation.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and readout
subsystems.role: compiles the circuit for a specific device, mitigates errors and extracts the result.

buildSteps.title: Define the task
buildSteps.detail: Decide the number of qubits n and the required phase precision, and whether this is a standalone QFT or the inverse subroutine inside phase estimation.

buildSteps.title: Write the gate sequence
buildSteps.detail: Start with Hadamard gates on all qubits, then apply controlled-phase gates whose rotation angles halve with each step, and finish with a swap network to restore qubit order. For the inverse, reverse the order and invert every gate.

buildSteps.title: Compile to hardware
buildSteps.detail: Map logical qubits onto physical qubits, insert SWAP gates to respect the device's connectivity, and translate each operation into the native gate set.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the gates
buildSteps.detail: Tune the microwave or laser pulses that implement single-qubit rotations and two-qubit controlled-phase gates, and measure their fidelities and coherence times.

buildSteps.title: Choose an error strategy
buildSteps.detail: On small devices use error mitigation such as zero-noise extrapolation; for larger instances encode the computation in an error-correcting code so that logical gates are protected.

buildSteps.title: Execute and read out
buildSteps.detail: Run the circuit many times, measure the qubits in the computational basis, and reconstruct the Fourier-transformed amplitudes or the estimated phase from the statistics.

buildSteps.title: Verify and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Compare results against a classical fast Fourier transform on small instances, then embed the verified circuit in a larger algorithm such as Shor's period finding or quantum phase estimation.

prerequisites.why: the QFT needs n qubits and controlled-phase interactions between many pairs; current devices have limited qubit counts and connectivity.
every controlled-phase gate is a two-qubit operation, and their errors accumulate quickly as n grows.
useful large-scale QFT requires logical qubits with error rates below the fault-tolerance threshold, which has not yet been achieved at scale.
the circuit must be translated, scheduled and driven on real hardware.
small instances can be checked against a classical FFT, which is essential for debugging.

pathway.milestone: QFT and phase estimation demonstrated on a handful of qubits on superconducting and trapped-ion devices
pathway.unlocks: proof that the gate sequence works and can be benchmarked.

pathway.milestone: QFT on tens of qubits with error mitigation, integrated into small instances of Shor's algorithm and quantum chemistry
pathway.unlocks: solving narrow problems beyond simple demonstration.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant QFT using a small number of logical qubits
pathway.unlocks: phase estimation precise enough for useful simulation of molecules and materials.

pathway.milestone: large-scale fault-tolerant QFT embedded in cryptographic and simulation algorithms
pathway.unlocks: exponentially faster period finding, factoring and related algebraic tasks.
